messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Bootstrapping using WLS estimator generates error: FAILED: creating sample statistics
parts: We are using WLS because our data failed to satisfy the normality condition.

If your endogenous variables have at least 5 categories, then ML provides results quite close to DWLS.  

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf

You can simply correct the SEs and test statistics for nonnormality by using robust estimation (e.g., estimator = "MLR").
And we need bootstrapping to report the confidence intervals and the p-value of the total, direct, and indirect effects in the mediation model.

If your sample size was large enough to entertain the possibility of using WLS, then it is certainly large enough for indirect effects to have an approximately normal sampling distribution.  So you should be able to trust the SEs reported in lavaan output, using the delta method.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

I think that's more than enough. If you read the literature recommending bootstrapping, the simulation studies on which they based that recommendation show discrepancies for samples N < 100, but negligible differences for larger samples.
